rules.intro.message: The Cape Verdean rules the app uses by default.

rules.try_tutorial.message: Learn by playing: try the tutorial
rules.try_tutorial.description: Link from the rules to the tutorial

rules.setup.1.message: The board has two rows of six pits. Each player owns the row nearest to them.

rules.setup.2.message: Each pit starts with 4 seeds, 48 in total. Each player has a store for captured seeds, which starts empty.

rules.setup.3.message: The first player is chosen at random. In a series, the loser of the previous game starts.

rules.sowing.1.message: On your turn, pick one of your own pits that has seeds.

rules.sowing.2.message: Take all of its seeds and drop them one at a time into each following pit, counter-clockwise: along your row to the right, then along your opponent’s row.

rules.sowing.3.message: Your pits are numbered 1 to 6 from your left.

rules.single_seed.1.message: You may not play a pit holding just 1 seed while any of your pits holds 2 or more.

rules.lap.1.message: With 12 or more seeds, the sowing laps the board and skips the pit you started from, which stays empty.
rules.lap.1.description: Rules section "Sowing 12 or more seeds", paragraph 1

rules.capture.1.message: If your last seed lands in an opponent’s pit and leaves it with exactly 2 or 3 seeds, you capture those seeds.

rules.capture.2.message: Chain capture: then check the pit just before it. If it is also on the opponent’s side and holds 2 or 3 seeds, capture it too. Keep going backwards until a pit doesn’t hold 2 or 3, or you reach your own side.

rules.capture.3.message: Captures are made whenever possible. A pit with 4 or more seeds is never captured.

rules.feeding.1.message: If your opponent has no seeds on their side, you must make a move that gives them at least one seed.

rules.feeding.2.message: If no move can feed them, the game ends and you collect the seeds left on your side.

rules.feeding.3.message: If the only move that feeds them is from a single-seed pit, feeding comes first and that move is allowed.

rules.grand_slam.1.message: A grand slam is a move that captures every seed on the opponent’s side. It is allowed, and you keep the seeds.

rules.grand_slam.2.message: You then play again immediately, and that extra move must leave the opponent at least one seed.

rules.grand_slam.3.message: If the grand slam already gives you 25 or more, you win at once.

rules.grand_slam.4.message: If the extra move can’t feed the opponent, the game ends and you collect the seeds on your side.

rules.end.1.message: A player who has captured 25 or more seeds wins at once. Seeds still on the board go to the player on whose side they are.
rules.end.1.description: Rules section "End of the game", paragraph 1

rules.end.2.message: The game also ends when no move can feed a starving opponent.
rules.end.2.description: Rules section "End of the game", paragraph 2

rules.end.3.message: Endless cycle: when a position repeats, or after 100 moves in a row without a capture, each player collects the seeds on their own side.
rules.end.3.description: Rules section "End of the game", paragraph 3

rules.end.4.message: Whoever has captured more seeds wins. 24–24 is a draw.
rules.end.4.description: Rules section "End of the game", paragraph 4

rules.end.5.message: Match play (optional): in a series, capturing 36 or more counts as a 2–0 win.
rules.end.5.description: Rules section "End of the game", paragraph 5

tutorial.opponent.description: Name of the opponent side in the tutorial

tutorial.back.description: Go to the previous tutorial step

tutorial.continue.description: Go to the next tutorial step

tutorial.sowing.intro.message: You play the bottom row. Tap your pit 3 (4 seeds) to sow its seeds one by one, counter-clockwise.
tutorial.sowing.intro.description: Tutorial step instruction before the move

tutorial.sowing.done.message: Each seed went into the next pit. The last one landed in the opponent’s pit 1, which now has 5, so nothing was captured.
tutorial.sowing.done.description: Tutorial step explanation after the move

tutorial.capture.intro.message: Play your pit 5. Its last seed will land in the opponent’s pit 1, which holds 1 seed.
tutorial.capture.intro.description: Tutorial step instruction before the move

tutorial.capture.done.message: The opponent’s pit ended with exactly 2 seeds, so you captured them. Pits ending with 2 or 3 are captured.
tutorial.capture.done.description: Tutorial step explanation after the move

tutorial.chain.intro.message: Play your pit 5 (3 seeds). Watch the opponent’s pits 1 and 2.
tutorial.chain.intro.description: Tutorial step instruction before the move

tutorial.chain.done.message: The last pit had 3, so it was captured, then the pit before it had 2, so it was captured too: 5 seeds in one move. The chain stops at your own side.
tutorial.chain.done.description: Tutorial step explanation after the move

tutorial.lap.intro.message: Your pit 1 has 12 seeds. Play it and watch what happens to the starting pit.
tutorial.lap.intro.description: Tutorial step instruction before the move

tutorial.lap.done.message: The sowing went all the way round and skipped the pit it started from, which stays empty.
tutorial.lap.done.description: Tutorial step explanation after the move

tutorial.single_seed.intro.message: Your pits 1 and 4 hold just 1 seed while others hold more, so they can’t be played. Play one of the highlighted pits.
tutorial.single_seed.intro.description: Tutorial step instruction before the move

tutorial.single_seed.done.message: Right. A pit with a single seed can only be played when none of your pits holds 2 or more.
tutorial.single_seed.done.description: Tutorial step explanation after the move

tutorial.feeding.intro.message: Your opponent has no seeds. You must give them at least one. Only one pit can reach their side: play it.
tutorial.feeding.intro.description: Tutorial step instruction before the move

tutorial.feeding.done.message: Your pit 6 fed the opponent. Your pit 2 couldn’t reach their side, so it wasn’t allowed. Feeding even beats the single-seed rule.
tutorial.feeding.done.description: Tutorial step explanation after the move

tutorial.grand_slam.intro.message: Play your pit 5 to capture every seed on the opponent’s side.
tutorial.grand_slam.intro.description: Tutorial step instruction before the move

tutorial.grand_slam.done.message: After a grand slam the extra move had to feed the opponent, so only your pit 6 was allowed.
tutorial.grand_slam.done.description: Tutorial step explanation after the move

tutorial.grand_slam.next.message: Grand slam! You play again, and this move must give the opponent a seed. Pits 4 and 6 both hold 1 seed: which one reaches their side?
tutorial.grand_slam.next.description: Tutorial: between the grand slam and the extra move

rules.continuous_relay.1.message: If your last seed lands in one of your own pits that already had seeds, pick up everything in it and keep sowing from the next pit.

rules.continuous_relay.2.message: This can happen several times in one move, even in the pit you started from.

rules.continuous_stop.1.message: The move ends when your last seed lands in an empty pit on your side, or anywhere on your opponent’s side, where the usual captures apply.

rules.continuous_other.1.message: No pit is ever skipped, not even the one you started from, however many seeds you sow.

rules.continuous_other.2.message: A lone seed can always be played.

rules.continuous_other.3.message: If your opponent has no seeds, your move must give them some during any lap. It still counts even if you then capture them all back.

home.heritage.world_cup.message: In 2026 the world met Cape Verde: on their World Cup debut, the Blue Sharks went unbeaten through their group, held Spain to a draw and took Argentina to extra time in the knockout round. Now it’s time to show the world more of our culture, starting with Ouril.
home.heritage.world_cup.description: Landing page heritage paragraph about Cape Verde's 2026 FIFA World Cup debut (facts checked July 2026: group draws with Spain 0-0, Uruguay 2-2, Saudi Arabia 0-0; lost 3-2 to Argentina after extra time in the round of 32)

variant.cv.across.about.message: You capture from the pit across from an empty pit of yours where your last seed lands, with a chain. Nothing is captured on your opponent’s side.

variant.cv.across-continuous.short.description: Rules option: capture across with continuous sowing

variant.cv.across-continuous.about.message: Capture across, with continuous sowing: sowing carries on from your occupied pits, and ends with a capture across when your last seed lands in an empty pit of yours.
variant.cv.across-continuous.about.description: Rules option description: capture across + continuous

rules.across.intro.message: Plays like Standard, except for how you capture.

rules.across_continuous.intro.message: Plays like Continuous sowing, except that you capture across.

rules.across_capture.1.message: If your last seed lands in an empty pit on your side and the pit across from it has seeds, you capture all of them, however many there are. The seed you dropped stays.

rules.across_capture.2.message: Then look at the pit you sowed just before. If it was empty too and the pit across has seeds, capture those as well, and keep going back until a pit doesn’t qualify or your row ends.

rules.across_capture.3.message: You never capture on your opponent’s side, not even on 2 or 3.

rules.across_continuous_end.title.description: Rules: capture across + continuous section title

rules.across_continuous_end.1.message: Sowing carries on from your occupied pits, so a move ends either in an empty pit of yours, where you can capture across, or on your opponent’s side, where nothing is captured.

rules.across_strategy.1.message: Don’t pile many seeds into one pit, because they can all be taken at once, and try to keep your opponent’s pits from running empty.

tutorial.across.intro.message: With the Capture across rules, you capture from your opponent’s pits facing yours. Play your pit 1 and drop a seed into each of your empty pits.
tutorial.across.intro.description: Tutorial step instruction before the move

tutorial.across.done.message: Your last seed landed in your empty pit 4, so you captured the seeds across from it. Pits 3 and 2 had been empty too, so the chain captured across from them as well. You’ve finished the tutorial!
tutorial.across.done.description: Tutorial step explanation after the move
